wal: use subordinating conjunctions to write complex sentences
tib: Complex sentences let me join two ideas together in a way that shows how they connect, making my writing more controlled.
isb: writing three paired complex sentences about scenes from Varjak’s first night, each using a different conjunction.

title: Grammar Warm-Up
subtitle: True or false? Decide whether each is a complex sentence and explain why.

cards.label: Sentence A
lines: Varjak crept forward and stopped at the corner.
Complex sentence? True or false?

cards.label: Sentence B
lines: Although it was dangerous,
Varjak crept out of the doorway.
Complex sentence? True or false?

cards.label: Sentence C
lines: He was afraid.
Complex sentence? True or false?

title: Recap: types of sentence
lines: A simple sentence has one main clause.
Varjak crept forward.
A compound sentence joins two main clauses with and, but, or, so.
Varjak crept forward but he could not see anything.
A complex sentence has a main clause and a subordinate clause,
joined by a subordinating conjunction.
Although it was dark, Varjak crept forward.
What makes a subordinate clause different from a main clause?

title: Subordinating conjunctions
right_lines: If the subordinate clause comes first,
Varjak crept out of the doorway.
If the main clause comes first,
Varjak crept out of the doorway

title: Paired sentences
lines: Here is one idea written two ways:
Although it was dangerous, Varjak crept out of the doorway.
Varjak crept out of the doorway, although it was dangerous.
Which changes the emphasis?
Which builds more tension?
Now try together:
Varjak heard a sound. He did not run away.
Can we rewrite this as one complex sentence,
two different ways?
Write three pairs of complex sentences.
Each pair should be about a different scene
from Varjak’s first night outside.
For each pair:
• Write the sentence with the subordinate clause first
• Write the same sentence with the main clause first
• Use a different conjunction for each pair
Then decide: which version of each pair
works better in the narrative, and why?
Be ready to share your best pair.

title: Share and discuss.
lines: Listen to a few pairs.
For each one, decide:
• Which version builds more tension?
• Is the comma in the right place?
• Which conjunction works best for that moment?
Which conjunction do you think
you will use most in your narrative?

q1: What is the difference between a coordinating conjunction and a subordinating conjunction?
q2: When does placing the subordinate clause first create more tension in a narrative?
q3: Which of your paired sentences do you want to use in your final write, and why?
